front open space for a residential plot.answer:
For a residential building up to 12.5 m in height, Rule 56(1)(a) fixes the minimum front open space by the width of the street facing the plot. A 9.0 m wide road falls in row 1 of that table — "Up to 9.0 meters" -> minimum front open space 3.0 meters. (The next row, 3.6 m, starts only for streets of MORE than 9.0 m and up to 12 m, so a road of exactly 9.0 m still gets 3.0 m.)

Two riders to keep in mind:
1. This 3.0 m applies only to buildings whose height is up to 12.5 m. If the building is higher than 12.5 m, Rule 56(5) sends you to Tables 4 and 5 of Rule 42, where the front M.O.S. is 7.5 m / 9.0 m / 12.0 m (above 12.5 m up to 30 m) and 15 m or more for high rise buildings — and those tables also require a minimum road width of 12 m and above, so a 9 m road will not support such a building under Table 4.
2. Rule 46 separately requires the building line to be set back at least 3 meters from the means of access, which is consistent with the 3.0 m figure here.

my plot is 200 sq m on a 9 m road. how m.answer:
**1. Front open space (setback)**
Rule 56(1)(a) gives front open space by width of the street facing the plot. Your road is 9.0 m, which falls in row 1 "Up to 9.0 meters" → **3.0 m minimum front open space**. (Rule 46 also requires the building line to be set back at least 3 m from the means of access, so 3.0 m is consistent.)

Related open spaces for a 200 sq m plot (building up to 12.5 m height):
- Rear open space, Rule 56(2)(a): plot "Above 150 and up to 225.00" sq m → **2.50 m**.
- Side open space, Rule 56(3): for a detached building 3.0 m on both sides (may be reduced to 1.5 m on one side if the building is up to 7 m high and the frontage is less than 12 m); for a semi-detached building 3.0 m on one side; for row-type buildings no side open space is required. Plot of 200 sq m can be semi-detached (125–225 sq m) or row type (50–225 sq m) under Rule 53(1).

**2. How many floors / how much construction**
The rules do not fix a number of floors; they fix height and FAR.
- Height: Rule 65(1) says height is governed by Tables 4 and 5 of Rule 42. Table 4 (buildings above 12.5 m and up to 30 m) needs a minimum plot of 1000 sq m on a 12 m road (row 1). Your 200 sq m plot on a 9 m road does not meet that, so you stay in the "up to 12.5 m height" category of Rule 56. Within 12.5 m, with the minimum habitable room height of 2.6 m (Rule 69(1)), the number of floors is whatever fits in 12.5 m — the rules state no floor count. A lift is required only for buildings more than 12.5 m (Rule 83).
- Built-up area (FAR): Rule 61, Table 8, Residential FAR = 1.25. Calculation: 200 sq m × 1.25 = **250 sq m of FAR built-up area**. (Areas excluded from FAR under Rule 2(30) are extra, but for an individual residence the excluded sum cannot exceed 25% of permissible FAR.) Rule 61 Note (3): on a plot of 200 to 500 sq m, one servant quarter up to 25 sq m is allowed and is not counted in built-up/covered area.

**3. Fees (Rule 21), worked out**
- Application fee, Rule 21(2)(ii): Rs 1.00 per sq m of proposed built-up area. If you build the full 250 sq m → 250 × Rs 1 = **Rs 250**.
- Permission fee, Rule 21(3)(b), item 1 (building used exclusively as residence), slab by built-up area:
  • 250 sq m falls in the row "201 – 300" → **Rs 3,000**.
  • (If you build only up to 200 sq m, the row "126 – 200" applies → Rs 2,000, and application fee Rs 200.)
- Total for 250 sq m residence: Rs 250 + Rs 3,000 = **Rs 3,250**, plus any development fees charged by the competent authority.
- If it is shop-cum-residence or commercial, add 50% to the item-1 fee (Rule 21(3)(b) items 2 and 4).

Also applicable: rain/roof water harvesting is compulsory for plots above 140 sq m (Rule 81(4)) and one tree per 100 sq m must be planted (Rule 67) before the occupancy certificate.

आपके प्लॉट (200 वर्ग मीटर) पर यदि भवन की ऊँचाई 12.5 मीटर तक है, तो नियम 56(1)(क) की तालिका लागू होगी।

गणना/तालिका पढ़ना:
- सड़क की चौड़ाई "9.0 मीटर तक" वाली पंक्ति → न्यूनतम सामने की खुली जगह (Front Open Space) = 3.0 मीटर।
- आपकी सड़क ठीक 9.0 मीटर है, अतः वह "Up to 9.0 meters" पंक्ति में ही आती है → 3.0 मीटर आगे छोड़ना होगा।
(यदि सड़क 9 मीटर से अधिक व 12 मीटर तक होती तो 3.6 मीटर, 12 से 18 मीटर तक 4.5 मीटर, और 18 मीटर से ऊपर 6.0 मीटर होती।)

साथ ही ध्यान रखें – नियम 56(2)(क) के अनुसार 150 से 225 वर्ग मीटर तक के प्लॉट पर पीछे (Rear) न्यूनतम 2.50 मीटर खुली जगह भी छोड़नी होगी।

यदि भवन की ऊँचाई 12.5 मीटर से अधिक प्रस्तावित हो, तो नियम 56(5) के अनुसार नियम 42 की तालिका 4/5 लागू होंगी (जिनमें न्यूनतम प्लॉट आकार 1000 वर्ग मीटर व 12 मीटर सड़क आवश्यक है), अतः 200 वर्ग मीटर/9 मीटर सड़क पर वह श्रेणी लागू नहीं होगी।

how much gap is needed at the back and o.answer:
**1) Rear and side open space (building up to 12.5 m height, residential) — Rule 56**

Rear Marginal Open Space depends on **plot area** (not road width) — Rule 56(2)(a):
- plot up to 40.00 sq m -> Nil
- above 40.00 and up to 150.00 sq m -> 1.50 m
- above 150 and up to 225.00 sq m -> 2.50 m
- above 225.00 sq m -> 3.00 m
The rear open space must run along the entire face of the rear wall (Rule 56(2)(b)).

Side Marginal Open Space depends on the **type of building** — Rule 56(3):
- Detached building: 3.0 m on both sides; relaxation: for a detached residential building up to 7 m height on a plot with frontage less than 12 m, one side may be reduced to 1.5 m.
- Semi-detached: 3.0 m on one side; for semi-detached up to 10 m height on a plot with frontage up to 10 m, it may be reduced to 2.5 m.
- Row-type building: no side open space required.

**2) Corner plots**
The rules do **not** give a separate rear/side setback table for corner sites (a "corner site" is only defined in Rule 2(19)). What does change for a plot touching more than one street is:
- Rear open space must still be provided through the entire face of the rear wall where a building abuts two or more streets — Rule 56(2)(b).
- Building height is regulated by the **wider** street — Rule 65(2).
- Boundary wall: on a corner plot the wall abutting the side road must also not exceed 1.5 m — Rule 78(b).

**3) Does the gap change with road width?**
- **Front** open space: yes. Rule 56(1)(a) table: road up to 9.0 m -> 3.0 m; more than 9.0 m and up to 12 m -> 3.6 m; more than 12.0 m and up to 18 m -> 4.5 m; above 18 m -> 6.0 m. (In existing developed areas with streets less than 6.0 m wide, the building line is taken 6.0 m from the centre line of the street — Rule 56(1)(b).)
- **Rear and side** for buildings up to 12.5 m: no, they go by plot area / building type as above.
- **Above 12.5 m height**: all the open spaces come from Tables 4 and 5 of Rule 42, which ARE road-width based (Rule 56(5)). E.g. Table 4, row 1: road 12.0 m and above, minimum plot 1000 sq m, frontage 18 m, FAR 1:1.50, height up to 18 m -> front MOS 7.5 m, sides/rear 6.0 m; row 2 (18 m road, 1500 sq m) -> 9.0 m front / 6.0 m sides; row 3 (24 m road, 2000 sq m) -> 12.00 m front / 7.5 m sides. High-rise buildings follow Table 5 (e.g. 30 m road -> front 15.00 m, sides/rear 7.5 m).

**4) Boundary wall / gate in the setback**
- A compound (boundary) wall is allowed and is governed by Rule 78: front compound wall max 1.5 m above the centre line of the front street (higher only if the Authority permits); rear and side compound walls max 3 m above the centre line of the service road where one exists, otherwise max 2 m; corner plot side-road wall max 1.5 m. Rule 78(c) exempts jails, electric sub-stations, institutional, hospital, industrial and educational buildings etc.
- Inside the marginal open space, Rule 58(1) says the open space must be kept free of construction and open to sky, except the listed items: cornice/weather shade up to 0.75 m, sunshade up to 0.75 m, projected balcony up to 1.20 m at first or higher floor with 1.5 m clearance from the plot boundary. Rule 58(4) additionally permits in the open spaces: a sanitary block (existing buildings, 2.4 m high, max 4 sq m, 1.5 m from rear boundary), a private garage not exceeding 25 sq m at the rear end of the side open space, and a pump room and watchman hut of up to 6.0 sq m each. Rule 56(4) also expressly allows a garage at the rear end of the side open space.
- Gate: for buildings other than residential, the main entrance to the plot must be at least 4.5 m wide and the gate must fold back against the compound wall, leaving the access way free for fire vehicles; if the entrance at the boundary wall is built over, clearance must be at least 4.5 m (Rule 41(c); same for buildings above 12.5 m / high rise under Rule 42(6)).

Only the FRONT setback changes with road width (3.0 / 3.6 / 4.5 / 6.0 m); above 12.5 m height everything comes from Rule 42 Tables 4-5. my plot is 200 sq m on a 9 m road. how m.answer:
**1) Front open space (Rule 56(1)(a), Table on p.77)**
For a residential building up to 12.5 m height, the front open space is read from the width of the street facing the plot. Your road is 9.0 m, so the row "Up to 9.0 meters -> 3.0 meters" applies: **leave 3.0 m front MOS**.
Related set-backs for a 200 sq m plot:
- Rear open space (Rule 56(2)(a)): row "Above 150 and up to 225.00 -> 2.50 m" = **2.50 m rear**.
- Side open space (Rule 56(3)): detached building = 3.0 m on both sides (one side may be reduced to 1.5 m if height is up to 7 m and frontage is less than 12 m); semi-detached = 3.0 m on one side (may be 2.5 m if height up to 10 m and frontage up to 10 m); row-type = no side open space. Which applies depends on your frontage (Rule 53(1)(i): 125-225 sq m = semi-detached with 8-12 m frontage; 50-225 sq m = row type with 4.5-12 m frontage).

**2) How many floors / how much can be built**
The rules do not fix a number of floors. They fix (a) FAR and (b) height:
- FAR: Rule 61, Table 8, row "Residential -> 1.25". Built-up area allowed = 1.25 x 200 sq m = **250 sq m**.
- Premium FAR (Rule 61, Note 7, inserted 6-3-2025): up to 25% of the Base FAR may be added on payment at a rate fixed by the State Government: 25% of 1.25 = 0.3125; 0.3125 x 200 = 62.5 sq m, i.e. a maximum of 250 + 62.5 = **312.5 sq m** with Premium FAR.
- Height: a building above 12.5 m is governed by Rule 42/Table 4, whose lowest row needs a minimum plot of 1000 sq m and a road of 12.0 m and above. Your plot (200 sq m) and road (9 m) do not meet that row, so **you cannot go above 12.5 m height** (Rule 65(1) read with Table 4).
- Practical effect (illustration only, your actual frontage decides): on a 10 m x 20 m plot as a semi-detached house, after 3.0 m front, 2.5 m rear and a 3.0 m side, the footprint is about (10-3) x (20-3-2.5) = 7 x 14.5 = 101.5 sq m; 250 sq m FAR / 101.5 sq m = about 2.5, i.e. roughly two full floors plus a part floor, within the 12.5 m height cap (minimum habitable room height 2.6 m, Rule 69(1)).

**3) Fees (Rule 21), taking 250 sq m built-up area**
- Application fee, Rule 21(2)(ii): Rs 1.00 per sq m of proposed built-up area = 250 x Rs 1 = **Rs 250**.
- Permission fee, Rule 21(3)(b), Item 1 (building used exclusively as residence), row "201 - 300 sq m" = **Rs 3,000**. (If you build only up to 200 sq m, the row "126 - 200" = Rs 2,000; if you use Premium FAR and cross 300 sq m, row "301 - 400" = Rs 4,000.)
- Total for 250 sq m: Rs 250 + Rs 3,000 = **Rs 3,250**, plus any development fee/charges levied by the competent authority and the Premium FAR rate fixed by the State Government if you use it.

**Other points for a 200 sq m plot**
- Instant/deemed approval under Rule 12A is only for residential plots up to 186 sq m, so your 200 sq m plot must go through normal building permission. However, Rule 6(3) allows a registered Architect/Structural Engineer to issue the permission for plots up to 300 sq m.
- Rule 67: one tree per 100 sq m, i.e. 2 trees, before the occupancy certificate.
- Rule 81(4): rain/roof water harvesting is compulsory as the plot exceeds 140 sq m.
- Rule 61, Note (4): covered parking of 2.4 m clear height within the permissible ground coverage is free of FAR on plots of 200 sq m or more - your plot just qualifies.

म र प ल ट 200 स क व यर म टर क ह और उसक आ.answer:
## 1. कितना गैप (खुली जगह / MOS) छोड़ना है

आपका प्लॉट **200 वर्गमीटर** है और सामने की सड़क **9.0 मीटर** चौड़ी है। ऊँचाई 12.5 मीटर तक मानते हुए नियम 56 लागू होगा:

### (क) सामने की खुली जगह (Front MOS) — नियम 56(1)

| सड़क की चौड़ाई | न्यूनतम सामने की खुली जगह |
|---|---|
| 9.0 मीटर तक | **3.0 मीटर** |
| 9.0 से 12 मीटर तक | 3.6 मीटर |
| 12 से 18 मीटर तक | 4.5 मीटर |
| 18 मीटर से ऊपर | 6.0 मीटर |

आपकी पंक्ति: **सड़क 9.0 मीटर तक → सामने 3.0 मीटर**

### (ख) पीछे की खुली जगह (Rear MOS) — नियम 56(2)

| प्लॉट क्षेत्रफल (वर्गमीटर) | न्यूनतम पीछे की खुली जगह |
|---|---|
| 40.00 तक | शून्य |
| 40.00 से ऊपर – 150.00 तक | 1.50 मीटर |
| 150 से ऊपर – 225.00 तक | **2.50 मीटर** |
| 225.00 से ऊपर | 3.00 मीटर |

आपकी पंक्ति: **200 वर्गमीटर (150–225 के बीच) → पीछे 2.50 मीटर**

### (ग) साइड की खुली जगह — नियम 53(1) + नियम 56(3)
200 वर्गमीटर प्लॉट नियम 53(1) के अनुसार **semi-detached (125–225 वर्गमीटर)** या **row type (50–225 वर्गमीटर)** श्रेणी में आता है — यह आपके निर्माण के प्रकार पर निर्भर है:

| निर्माण का प्रकार | साइड खुली जगह |
|---|---|
| Semi-detached | एक तरफ **3.0 मीटर**; (ऊँचाई 10 मी. तक + फ्रंटेज 10 मी. तक हो तो **2.5 मीटर** तक घटाई जा सकती है) |
| Row type | कोई साइड खुली जगह आवश्यक नहीं |
| Detached (225 वर्गमीटर से ऊपर के प्लॉट पर) | दोनों तरफ 3.0 मीटर |

**संक्षेप: आगे 3.0 मी., पीछे 2.50 मी., साइड (semi-detached होने पर) 3.0 मी. (शर्त पूरी होने पर 2.5 मी.), row type में साइड शून्य।**

---

## 2. फीस की गणना

फीस दो हिस्सों में लगती है (नियम 21):

**(क) आवेदन फीस** = प्रस्तावित निर्मित क्षेत्र (built‑up area) का **₹1.00 प्रति वर्गमीटर**।

**(ख) अनुमति फीस (Permission Fee)** — केवल आवासीय भवन के लिए स्लैब:

| निर्मित क्षेत्र (वर्गमीटर) | फीस |
|---|---|
| 126 – 200 | ₹2,000 |
| 201 – 300 | ₹3,000 |
| 301 – 400 | ₹4,000 |

### उदाहरण गणना (आवासीय, FAR 1.25 — नियम 61)
- अधिकतम अनुमेय निर्मित क्षेत्र = 200 वर्गमीटर × 1.25 = **250 वर्गमीटर**
- आवेदन फीस = 250 × ₹1 = **₹250**
- अनुमति फीस (250 वर्गमीटर → 201–300 स्लैब) = **₹3,000**
- **कुल = ₹250 + ₹3,000 = ₹3,250**

यदि आप कम निर्माण करते हैं, मान लीजिए 180 वर्गमीटर:
- आवेदन फीस = 180 × ₹1 = ₹180
- अनुमति फीस (126–200 स्लैब) = ₹2,000
- **कुल = ₹2,180**

*(दुकान/व्यावसायिक या shop‑cum‑residence हो तो उपरोक्त फीस पर 50% अतिरिक्त लगेगा। इसके अलावा सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा लागू विकास शुल्क अलग से देय होगा — नियम 12A(7).)*

---

## 3. दो और बातें जो इस प्लॉट पर लागू होंगी
- **वर्षा जल संचयन** अनिवार्य है (140 वर्गमीटर से बड़े प्लॉट पर) — नियम 81(4)।
- **वृक्षारोपण**: प्रति 100 वर्गमीटर एक पेड़ → आपके 200 वर्गमीटर पर **2 पेड़** — नियम 67।
- 200 वर्गमीटर प्लॉट पर एक नौकर कक्ष (25 वर्गमीटर तक) तथा ढका हुआ पार्किंग FAR में नहीं गिना जाता — नियम 61 के नोट (3) व (4)।

fees for extra floor.answer:
## Fee for adding an extra floor (addition/alteration that increases built-up area)

Adding a floor is an "alteration" (Rule 2(3)) and needs fresh building permission under Rule 12(1). Two fees are payable:

**1. Application fee — Rule 21(2)(ii)**
> Rs. 1.00 per square metre of the proposed built-up area.

**2. Permission fee — Rule 21(3)(b), Item 1 (purely residential building), slab table:**

| Built-up area from (sq.m.) | to (sq.m.) | Fee (Rs.) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 75 | 750 |
| 76 | 125 | 1,250 |
| 126 | 200 | 2,000 |
| 201 | 300 | 3,000 |
| 301 | 400 | 4,000 |
| 401 | 600 | 6,000 |
| 601 | 750 | 7,500 |
| 751 | 1,000 | 10,000 |
| 1,001 | 1,250 | 12,500 |
| 1,251 | 1,500 | 15,000 |
| 1,501 | 2,000 | 20,000 |
| 2,001 | 2,500 | 25,000 |
| above 2,500 | — | 50,000 |

- Shops / store house / factory / trade / other commercial or industrial (Item 2) and shop-cum-residence (Item 4): **fee of Item 1 + an additional 50%**.
- If the building is a **high rise** (more than 10 storeys or more than 30 m — Rule 2(38)), Rule 21(3)(c) Item 1 applies instead: **Rs. 10.00 per sq.m. of built-up area** (commercial +100%, shop-cum-residence +50%).

**Worked example (residential, extra floor of 150 sq.m.):**
1. Application fee = 150 sq.m. × Rs. 1.00 = **Rs. 150**
2. Permission fee, if reckoned on the 150 sq.m. of new built-up area → slab 126–200 → **Rs. 2,000**
3. Total = Rs. 150 + Rs. 2,000 = **Rs. 2,150**

*(If your office reckons the slab on the total built-up area of the whole building after addition — e.g. 150 existing + 150 new = 300 sq.m. → slab 201–300 → Rs. 3,000 — the figure changes; the rule states the slab against "built up area" without expressly saying new-only or total. Decide as per your office practice.)*

### Two special lower-fee entries (they do NOT cover a new floor)
- **Item 7 – Rs. 500**: only for external addition/alteration **which does not add to the built-up area** (courtyard, compound wall, elevation change, roofing change, openings).
- **Item 8 – Rs. 500**: addition/alteration **in the proposed (not yet executed) plan up to 10%**; above 10% a **fresh application** under the rules is necessary.

### Other points for an upper floor
- **No fresh Nazul NOC** is needed for upper floors if the ground floor was already approved (Rule 16(11)(c), second proviso).
- The extra floor must stay within permissible FAR (Rule 61, Table 8 — residential 1.25), ground coverage, height and MOS norms (Rules 42, 56).
- If the floor was already built without/beyond permission, Rule 24 applies: deviation exceeding **30% of permissible FAR** is not permissible, and the local body may charge a **compounding fee** under its own Act/rules (Rule 24(3)) — that compounding fee is not fixed by these rules.

**आपका प्रश्न स्पष्ट नहीं है, और "1 मीटर का प्लॉट" जैसी कोई स्थिति म.प्र. भूमि विकास नियम, 2012 में नहीं दी गई है।**

कृपया काउंटर पर निम्न जानकारी दें, तभी सही नियम बताया जा सकता है:

| आवश्यक जानकारी | उदाहरण |
|---|---|
| प्लॉट का क्षेत्रफल (वर्ग मीटर में) | जैसे 100 वर्ग मीटर |
| प्लॉट की चौड़ाई (frontage) व गहराई | जैसे 10 मी. × 15 मी. |
| सामने की सड़क की चौड़ाई | जैसे 9.0 मी. |
| प्रस्तावित उपयोग | आवासीय / व्यावसायिक / औद्योगिक आदि |
| प्रस्तावित भवन की ऊँचाई / मंज़िलें | जैसे 2 मंज़िल |
| नगर/क्षेत्र (विकास योजना लागू है या नहीं) | भोपाल – विकास योजना क्षेत्र |

यदि आपका आशय यह है कि प्लॉट का क्षेत्रफल केवल 1 वर्ग मीटर है, तो इस आकार के भूखंड पर निर्माण/अनुज्ञा के संबंध में इन नियमों में कोई प्रावधान नहीं मिलता — यह उत्तर म.प्र. भूमि विकास नियम, 2012 में उपलब्ध नहीं है। सही आँकड़े मिलने पर न्यूनतम भूखंड आकार, खुली जगह (MOS), FAR व भवन अनुज्ञा शुल्क की गणना करके बताई जा सकती है।

what are the rules for plots up to 500 s.answer:
The rules don't have one single "plots up to 500 sq m" rule – the 500 sq m figure appears in several separate places, and a small plot is also governed by the ordinary residential development-control rules. Here is the consolidated picture for a residential plot of **up to 500 sq m**.

## A. Where "500 sq m" is expressly mentioned

| Provision | What it says for plots up to 500 sq m |
|---|---|
| Rule 22(A)(2)(1)(b) – merger | Contiguous residential plots may be merged, but the **merged plot must not exceed 500 sq m** (EWS/LIG plots cannot be merged at all) |
| Rule 26(9)(A)(b) – Architect | An Architect may submit **structural details and calculations for residential buildings on a plot up to 500 sq m and up to three storeys / 11 m** |
| Rule 26(9)(B)(i) – Structural Engineer | May submit **all plans and information for residential buildings on plots up to 500 sq m and up to three storeys / 11 m** |
| Rule 26(9)(C)(ii) – Engineer | May submit **structural details and calculation for all buildings on plots up to 500 sq m and height up to four storeys (15 m)** |
| Rule 61, Note (3) – servant quarter | Plot **200–500 sq m → one servant quarter**; more than 500 sq m → two. Size not to exceed 25 sq m; not counted in built-up/covered area |

## B. Simplified permission routes for smaller plots

| Plot size | Facility |
|---|---|
| Up to 186 sq m (residential) | Rule 12-A **instant / deemed approval** on an individual plot (not for colonisers), on the Appendix A-2(2) form + affidavit + Rule 21 fee |
| Up to 300 sq m | Rule 6(3): a registered **Architect/Structural Engineer may issue the building permission** (with Director's approval); Rule 21(4): **standard approved building plans** are kept by the Authority and the fee receipt is treated as the permission |

## C. Ordinary development control that applies to such a plot

- **Plot type / frontage (Rule 53(1))**: Row type 50–225 sq m (frontage 4.5–12 m); Semi-detached 125–225 sq m (8–12 m); Detached above 225 sq m (above 12 m).
- **Front open space (Rule 56(1)(a), height up to 12.5 m)**:

| Width of street facing the plot | Minimum front open space |

**यह जानकारी म.प्र. भूमि विकास नियम, 2012 में उपलब्ध नहीं है।**

आपका प्रश्न निर्माण सामग्री में मिलावट (cement में रेती/बालू मिलाना) करने वाले ठेकेदार पर लगने वाले **दंड/penalty** के बारे में है। इन नियमों में ऐसी किसी मिलावट के लिए कोई जुर्माना, सज़ा या कार्यवाही निर्धारित नहीं की गई है।

ये नियम केवल विकास अनुमति, भवन अनुमति, खुली जगह, FAR, पार्किंग आदि से संबंधित हैं। सामग्री की गुणवत्ता के बारे में सामान्य अपेक्षा तो है, पर उल्लंघन पर दंड का प्रावधान इन नियमों में नहीं दिया गया — अतः इस प्रश्न का उत्तर इन नियमों से नहीं दिया जा सकता।

**आगे क्या करें:** गुणवत्ता/मिलावट की शिकायत ठेके (contract) की शर्तों, संबंधित नगर पालिक निगम अधिनियम/उपभोक्ता कानून या पुलिस में धोखाधड़ी के प्रावधानों के अंतर्गत देखी जाएगी — वह इस काउंटर के दायरे से बाहर है।

parking rules for commercial.answer:
**Short answer:** The general parking norms are kept in **Appendix I-1 and I-2** (Rule 84), which are *not* part of the rule text supplied to this tool. However, the rules themselves fix parking for specific commercial buildings — **shopping malls / open malls (Rule 96)** and **multiplexes (Rule 95)** — plus the way parking area is converted into "equivalent car spaces".

---

### 1. General provision — Rule 84
- Rule 84(1): parking on the plot and off the plot is to be as per **Appendix I-1 and I-2**.
- Rule 84(2): a **standalone multi-level public parking** is permissible in residential, commercial, PSP, industrial, recreational, agriculture and transportation land use; **5% of its built-up area may be used for commercial activity**, with front MOS 12 m, all other sides 7.5 m, ground coverage max 80%.

### 2. Shopping Mall / Open Mall — Rule 96 (applies only where the Development Plan is silent)

| Town population | Shopping Mall | Open Mall |
|---|---|---|
| Up to 3 lakhs | 1 car space per 60 sq m built-up area | 1 car space per 60 sq m built-up area |
| 3 to 5 lakhs | 1 car space per 55 sq m built-up area | 1 car space per 55 sq m built-up area |
| Above 5 lakhs | **1 car space per 50 sq m built-up area** | **1 car space per 50 sq m built-up area** |

*(Bhopal is above 5 lakhs → the 50 sq m row applies.)*

**Rule 96(2) – equivalent car space calculation:**

| Type of space | Divide by |
|---|---|
| Basement (sq m) | 35 sq m |
| Over-ground covered parking (podium / stilt) (sq m) | 50 sq m |
| Open spaces (sq m) | 25 sq m |

### 3. Multiplex / Multiplex-cum-shopping — Rule 95 (again, only where the Development Plan is silent)

| Town population | Multiplex | Multiplex-cum-shopping |
|---|---|---|
| Up to 3 lakhs | 1 car space per 55 sq m built-up area | 1 car space per 55 sq m built-up area |
| 3.0 to 7.5 lakhs | 1 car space per 50 sq m built-up area | 1 car space per 50 sq m built-up area |
| Above 7.5 lakhs | 1 car space per 45 sq m built-up area | 1 car space per 45 sq m built-up area |

Conversion of an old cinema to a multiplex: if the number of seats does not increase, **no additional parking**; if seats increase, extra parking **@ one car space for every 12 seats** [Rule 95 Note (c)].

**Rule 95(5) – equivalent car space calculation:** basement ÷ 35 sq m; over-ground covered parking ÷ 30 sq m; open spaces ÷ 25 sq m; **no parking is allowed in the marginal open spaces (MOS)**.

*Worked example:* a mall in Bhopal (above 5 lakhs) with 6,000 sq m built-up area → 6,000 ÷ 50 = **120 equivalent car spaces** required.

### 4. Related points for commercial buildings
- **Open spaces (Rule 57(d))** for business/mercantile/storage buildings: 6 m front, 4.5 m on the other three sides. The reported High Court comment stresses that 4.5 m off-street parking and 4.5 m open space are **two separate requirements and cannot be clubbed**.
- **Basement** may be used for parking spaces [Rule 76(3)(d)].
- **Parking floors**: on plots of **not less than 1000 sq m**, covered parking with clear height not more than 2.4 m is allowed on any floor and is **not counted in FAR** (Rule 63); podium parking similarly excluded (Rule 62).
- Rule 61 Note (4): covered parking (clear height 2.4 m) within permissible ground coverage on plots of **200 sq m or more** is not counted in FAR or height.

## Setbacks (marginal open spaces) for a 200 sq m residential plot, building height up to 12.5 m — Rule 56

**1. Front open space — depends on the width of the street facing the plot (Rule 56(1)(a)):**

| Width of street facing the plot | Minimum front open space |
|---|---|
| Up to 9.0 m | **3.0 m** |
| More than 9.0 m and up to 12 m | 3.6 m |

| Above 18 m | 6.0 m |

Special case: in existing developed areas where the street is **less than 6.0 m wide**, the building line must be **6.0 m from the centre line of the street** (Rule 56(1)(b)).

**2. Rear open space — depends on plot area (Rule 56(2)(a)):**

| Plot area (sq m) | Minimum rear open space |
|---|---|
| Up to 40.00 | Nil |
| Above 40.00 and up to 150.00 | 1.50 m |
| Above 150 and up to 225.00 | **2.50 m** |
| Above 225.00 | 3.00 m |

200 sq m falls in the band "Above 150 and up to 225.00" → **rear MOS 2.50 m**.

**3. Side open space — depends on the type of building (Rule 56(3)):**

| Type of building | Side open space |
|---|---|
| Detached | 3.0 m on **both** sides (may be reduced to 1.5 m on one side if height up to 7 m and frontage less than 12 m) |
| Semi-detached | 3.0 m on **one** side (may be reduced to 2.5 m if height up to 10 m and frontage up to 10 m) |
| Row type | **Nil** |

Under Rule 53(1)(i), a 200 sq m plot is normally a **semi-detached** (125–225 sq m, frontage 8–12 m) or **row-type** (50–225 sq m, frontage 4.5–12 m) plot; "detached" is prescribed for plots above 225 sq m.

### Typical answer at the counter (semi-detached house, 9 m road, height ≤ 12.5 m)
- Front: **3.0 m**
- Rear: **2.50 m**
- Side: **3.0 m on one side** (2.5 m if height ≤ 10 m and frontage ≤ 10 m)

If the building exceeds 12.5 m in height, Rule 56(5) sends you to Tables 4 and 5 of Rule 42 instead (those tables also require a minimum plot of 1000 sq m and above, so they do not fit a 200 sq m plot).

what is the far for residential.answer:
## Short answer
Under **Rule 61, Table 8**, the Floor Area Ratio for the **Residential** use group is **1.25**.

### Rule 61 – Table 8 (FAR for different use groups)

| S.No. | Use Group | FAR* | Category |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Residential | **1.25** | – |
| 2 | Commercial | 2.50 | City Centre |
| 2 | Commercial | 2.00 | Sub-city centre |
| 2 | Commercial | 1.75 | Community Center |
| 2 | Commercial | 1.50 | Local Shopping Centre |
| 2 | Commercial | 1.25 | Convenience Shopping Centre |
| 3 | Public Semi-public | 1.00 | Administrative Areas / Education and Research / Health / Social / Cultural / Institutional |
| 4 | Industrial | as per rule 48 | as per rule 48 |

\* "F.A.R and Density may be adopted as provided in the Development Plans of respective towns."

**Worked example:** plot of 200 sq m x FAR 1.25 = **250 sq m** of permissible built-up area (built-up area being computed as per the inclusions/exclusions in Rule 2(30)).

## But other provisions point differently – the clerk must decide which applies

1. **Rule 42, Table 4 (height above 12.5 m up to 30 m)** – FAR is fixed by road width, not by the 1.25 figure:

| Road width | Min. plot/land area | Frontage | FAR | Building height | Front MOS | Side/rear MOS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12.0 m and above | 1000 sq m | 18 m | 1:1.50 | up to 18 m | 7.5 m | 6.0 m |
| 18 m and above | 1500 sq m | 21 m | 1:1.75 | up to 24 m | 9.0 m | 6.0 m |
| 24 m and above | 2000 sq m | 30 m | 1:2.0 | up to 30 m | 12.00 m | 7.5 m |

2. **Rule 42, Table 5 (high rise buildings)** – FAR from 1:2.25 (30 m road) up to 1:3.0 (60 m / 75 m roads).

3. **Rule 60, Table 7 (Group Housing)** – FAR is tied to gross residential density: 125 persons/ha -> 0.75; 250 -> 1.25; 425 -> 1.50; 500 -> 1.75; 625 -> 2.00, "unless otherwise provided in the development plan".

4. **Rule 61, Note (7)** – a **Premium FAR not exceeding 25% of the Base FAR** may be allowed over and above the table (rate to be decided by the State Government). On a base of 1.25 that is an extra 0.3125, i.e. up to 1.5625 in total.

5. **Rule 61 footnote \*** and **Rule 103** – the Development Plan of the town may prescribe a different FAR/density, and Rule 103 gives the development plan precedence (with the Director referring contrary cases to Government).

So: **1.25 is the base residential FAR under Rule 61**, but for buildings taller than 12.5 m the Rule 42 road-width tables apply, for group housing the Rule 60 density table applies, Premium FAR may add up to 25%, and the local Development Plan may override.
